findings.claim: The diff declares `mod control_transport;` and imports `ControlTransport`/`ControlResponse`/`TransportFailure` from it in doctor.rs and kbd.rs, but no `control_transport.rs` file appears anywhere in the packet — if this packet is the complete change, the crate does not compile.
findings.evidence: mod.rs hunk adds `mod control_transport;`; doctor.rs adds `use super::control_transport::ControlTransport;`; kbd.rs adds `use super::control_transport::{ControlResponse, ControlTransport, TransportFailure};` — yet the diff contains no `diff --git` entry creating `tools/prometheus-cli/crates/prometheus-cli/src/commands/control_transport.rs`. Criterion 1.1 ('Add managed Unix-socket HTTP transport') is checked but its artifact is absent from the change.
findings.suggested_fix: Include `control_transport.rs` (with the Unix-socket default transport, PROMETHEUS_CONTROL_ENDPOINT override, and GET/POST tests) in the change, or verify it is already committed and rebase the packet so the change is self-contained.

findings.claim: The position.json rewrite silently drops the entire tracked phase tree — ~40 phases including PENDING ones (cowork-integration, goal-loop-support, phase-codex-plugin-implementation, phase-bdd-video-proof, machine-installation-2026-05-25, etc.) — collapsing root progress from done 142/total 194 to done 0/total 1, and nothing in the acceptance criteria or 'What Changes' authorizes deleting that orchestration state.
findings.evidence: position.json hunk removes 2300+ lines of phase/change nodes and leaves only `openspec-mirror-drift-cleanup` with one child; root.progress changes from {"done": 142, "total": 194} to {"done": 0, "total": 1}. The new position-reminder.txt states the counter is 'a PROJECT-WIDE roll-up across every phase in canonical state' and reports '0 of 1 (implementation, ALL phases)', confirming the other phases are gone from canonical state, not merely hidden. The change scope lists only transport, signer, partial-authority, and child/stage-gate seam repairs.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full phase tree in the canonical journal/projection, or if this pruning is an intentional migration, document it in the change and verify every consumer of position.json tolerates the missing phases.

findings.claim: current-waypoint.json removes eight previously-present keys (`stage`, `nextCommand`, `certificationStatus`, `publicationStatus`, `previousPhase`, `nextPendingChange`, `parentPhase`, `childPhases`, `changesCompleted/changesTotal`) while keeping schemaVersion "5", so any hook or script reading those fields now gets absent values with no schema signal.
findings.evidence: The waypoint hunk deletes `"stage": "execute_complete"`, `"nextCommand": "/kbd-new-phase kbd-control-plane-recovery"`, `"certificationStatus": "PASS"`, `"publicationStatus": "COMPLETE"`, `"previousPhase"`, `"childPhases": []`, etc., yet emits `"schemaVersion": "5"` unchanged. The repo contains waypoint consumers (e.g. scripts/check-waypoint-staleness.sh, scripts/validate-kbd-state.js) whose field expectations cannot be confirmed from this packet.
findings.suggested_fix: Either bump schemaVersion and migrate consumers, or verify every reader of the removed fields tolerates their absence; also note criterion 5.1 requires restoring exact next command `/kbd-new-phase kbd-control-plane-recovery`, which the current `exactNextCommand` (`/kbd-assess ...`) does not yet reflect.

findings.claim: `child_label="$(kbd_node_chain ...)"` was moved above the point where `runtime_lib` (`shared/lib/runtime-authority.sh`) is located and sourced, so if `kbd_node_chain` is defined in that library the script now dies with command-not-found under `set -e` before ever reaching activation.
findings.evidence: The hunk inserts the `kbd_node_chain` call immediately after the scope.json write (line ~129) and before `runtime_lib="$KBD_ORCHESTRATOR_ROOT/shared/lib/runtime-authority.sh"`; the previous call site at line ~230 was safely after that block. The diff does not include the definition of `kbd_node_chain`, so availability at the new call site is unverifiable — and criterion 3.1 only claims syntax check plus child creation passed, which would not exercise a runtime-authority-sourced helper if that path wasn't taken.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm `kbd_node_chain` is defined in the script header or an earlier-sourced library; if it lives in runtime-authority.sh, move the helper into the script or source the lib before computing the label, and add a test that exercises the runtime-authority branch of child creation.

findings.claim: If `~/.config/sovereign-sync/device-key.json` exists but is corrupt or unreadable, `load_device_key` returns an error that now propagates with no fallback to the platform credential store, regressing every managed-canonical runtime that previously signed successfully.
findings.evidence: In the device signer selection: `if let Some(path) = managed_device_key_path().filter(|path| path.is_file()) { return load_device_key(&path); }` — the `return` short-circuits before `KeyStorage::PlatformCredentialStore => self.platform_device_signer()`. A stale or malformed file (e.g. partial write, old enrollment) hard-fails signing instead of falling back to the identity that worked before this change.
findings.suggested_fix: On `load_device_key` failure for the discovered managed path, log the error and fall through to `platform_device_signer()`, or validate the key against the enrolled daemon identity before committing to it.

findings.claim: Replacing the startup `bail!` on failed project opens with a `warn!` removes the only retry mechanism: a transient open failure (e.g. volume not yet mounted at boot) now leaves that project's routes permanently unavailable until a manual daemon restart, whereas launchd previously restarted the service and retried.
findings.evidence: rest_api.rs hunk replaces `anyhow::bail!("{failed} registered local authorit{} failed to open", ...)` with a `warn!(... "healthy project routes remain available")` and proceeds to `Ok::<_, anyhow::Error>(kbd_projects)`; no re-open or reconciliation loop for failed registrations is added anywhere in the diff. Criterion 5.1 explicitly retains 'stale-registry' as a residual risk.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a periodic or on-demand re-open attempt for failed registrations (e.g. retry on first route access or a background reconciler), or document the restart-to-recover requirement in the operator-facing log message.

findings.claim: The new discovery test covers only PlatformCredentialStore with custom vs managed roots; it never asserts that a LegacyRuntimeFile runtime under the managed root is excluded, and it silently skips its positive assertion when `dirs_next::data_local_dir()` returns None.
findings.evidence: `managed_device_key_discovery_is_limited_to_the_default_canonical_data_root` builds both fixtures with `key_storage: KeyStorage::PlatformCredentialStore` and wraps the managed-root assertion in `if let Some(data_root) = dirs_next::data_local_dir()`, so in an environment without a data dir the test passes having asserted only the negative case.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a LegacyRuntimeFile + managed-root case, and fail loudly (or construct a synthetic root) when `data_local_dir()` is None instead of skipping.
